metadata.note: The L&N's 'Short Line' between Louisville and Cincinnati -- the northern leg of the through Cincinnati-New Orleans route (see nashville_lines.geojson for the Louisville-Nashville continuation of the same trains). Built by the Louisville, Cincinnati and Lexington Railroad/Railway: the LaGrange-Covington cutoff opened June 1869, and through rail service to Cincinnati followed on April 1, 1872 when the Newport & Cincinnati Bridge (soon renamed the L&N Railroad Bridge) opened as the first rail crossing of the Ohio River at Cincinnati. The L&N purchased the whole railroad in 1881. Passed through LaGrange, Eminence, Corinth/Williamstown, Walton, and Latonia/Covington before crossing the river; still operates today as CSX's LCL Subdivision, nicknamed the 'Short Line' since the 1870s. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: traced through real track geometry using OpenStreetMap data (Overpass API) and a shortest-path graph search chaining real way segments together, following the still-active CSX alignment, terminating at Cincinnati Union Terminal (opened 1933; the L&N used earlier downtown Cincinnati depots before that, not individually traced here). The traced length (184.5 km / 114.6 mi) runs a bit longer than the commonly cited Covington-Louisville mileage (101.4-103 mi), consistent with the added distance of continuing across the river into downtown Cincinnati rather than stopping at Covington.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_People_Bridge (Newport & Cincinnati Bridge opened April 1, 1872, first Ohio River rail bridge at Cincinnati; renamed the L&N Railroad Bridge in 1904; rail traffic removed 1984)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for the pre-Pan-American era (1872-1921); precise downtown Cincinnati depot(s) used before Union Terminal opened in 1933; whether any successor Amtrak service ever again reached Cincinnati over this line (none found -- the 1971 Floridian's northern end was Chicago, not Cincinnati, so this segment appears to have lost all passenger service in 1971 with no later revival).
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API), railway=rail ways, for the still-active CSX LCL Subdivision alignment, chained via shortest-path graph search between Louisville and Cincinnati Union Terminal
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
